title: Recover the run, not just the process
description: Inject a production failure, then choose state, retry, trace, and deployment controls. The incident tape shows what survives and what can safely resume.

stateOptions.label: Durable checkpointer
stateOptions.detail: Thread state and pending writes survive worker replacement.

retryOptions.label: Replay the whole run
retryOptions.detail: Start from admission and repeat every completed stage.

retryOptions.label: Retry the failed boundary
retryOptions.detail: Resume at the failed model or tool call under the original deadline.

retryOptions.label: Reconcile, then resume
retryOptions.detail: Read authoritative state before deciding whether a side effect needs another attempt.

observabilityOptions.label: Root request log
observabilityOptions.detail: One final status with no child-stage evidence.

observabilityOptions.label: Nested step traces
observabilityOptions.detail: Correlated model, tool, checkpoint, release, and effect evidence.

deploymentOptions.label: Scale-to-zero function
deploymentOptions.detail: Request compute may disappear while background or waiting work remains.

deploymentOptions.label: Single application host
deploymentOptions.detail: API admission and execution share one scaling and restart boundary.

deploymentOptions.label: API plus durable workers
deploymentOptions.detail: Admission and queued execution scale independently.

incidents.label: Refund response lost
incidents.brief: The payment service may have committed, but the worker dies before recording the response.
incidents.safeOutcome: Lookup by operation key, record the existing refund, and resume without a second effect.
incidents.unsafeOutcome: The refund is replayed as a new operation and the customer can receive two credits.

incidents.label: Model rate limit
incidents.brief: A transient 429 occurs before the model returns any output.
incidents.safeOutcome: Retry only the model call with jitter inside the original deadline and quota budget.
incidents.unsafeOutcome: Whole-run replay repeats retrieval and admission work, amplifying load during a provider incident.

incidents.label: Deploy during approval
incidents.brief: A run waits for human approval while a new application revision replaces its worker.
incidents.effect: The approved action has not run
incidents.safeOutcome: Load the checkpoint with a compatible revision and resume after the approval boundary.
incidents.unsafeOutcome: The waiting run is orphaned or restarted from admission, losing the original approval context.

incidents.label: Client stream disconnect
incidents.brief: The user disconnects while a long-running research run continues in the background.
incidents.effect: Work is still running after delivery fails
incidents.safeOutcome: Keep the run durable, expose its status by run ID, and let the client reconnect without duplicating execution.
incidents.unsafeOutcome: The request process is treated as the run owner, so disconnect causes lost work or a duplicate restart.
